title: SDK first-day rituals and experiments (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures an experiential, time-boxed "first day" flow for new developers trying the Redwood SDK for the very first time. The goal is to define a 60–90 minute guided lab (or self-serve checklist) that sets a new user up with a working integration, teaches key debugging rituals, surfaces cost/latency tradeoffs, and leaves them with a repeatable pattern they can use in production rollouts.

Why 'rituals'?:
We observed that teams who adopt small, repeated habits during onboarding (e.g., verifying keys with a short smoke call, pinning a model version, and running a latency budget test) have lower first-week support tickets. This doc suggests concrete steps and short experiments (with expected outcomes) to form those habits.

Target personas:
- ML/Infra engineer evaluating runtime performance of model endpoint.
- Product engineer implementing a chat feature with Redwood hosted API.
- Platform engineer validating Dedicated routing and quota behavior.

Timeboxed flow (60–90 minutes) — high level
1) 0–10 min: Hello world + identity check
   - Ritual: run a single minimal text-generation call that returns within the console.
   - Expected: successful 200 + JSON stream or final response; event in telemetry (event: "sdk_onramp_smoke").
   - Failure modes to check: auth 401, region mismatch 409, malformed JSON 422.
   - Microcopy examples for error screens: "API key invalid — check clipboard + active workspace"; "Region mismatch — try setting REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2".

2) 10–25 min: Pin a model, run a latency baseline
   - Ritual: pin a specific model version in the local config (e.g., model: open-mpt-7b/2025-03) and run 20 short requests (prompt length < 50 tokens) to measure p50/p95.
   - Artifacts: small CSV with columns [timestamp, latency_ms, status_code, tokens_out].
   - Expected outcome: p50 < 120ms for hosted tier (subject to model/region).
   - Notes: record a small snippet in the console explaining why pinning matters for deterministic rollouts.

3) 25–45 min: Simulate burst and fallback behavior
   - Ritual: increase concurrency locally (or use provided load script) to trigger autoscaling/burst policy in Dedicated or force a fallback to cheaper variant.
   - Experiment steps: start with 1 req/sec, increase to 20 req/sec for 30s, then back down.
   - Observables: routing header (X-RDW-Route), model-variant switch log, fallback_reason in trace.
   - Acceptance: app gracefully receives responses and logs contain fallback_reason when triggered.

4) 45–60 min: Cost/quality spot-check (batching + quantization toggle)
   - Ritual: flip a single config: enable batching=on and quant_profile=8bit-fast, run the same prompt set and compare token-per-second and perceptual differences.
   - Quick pass metric: tokens/s improved by >15% with <5% quality regression on our sample prompts.
   - Operational note: capture a screenshot of the Console per-route cost breakdown and attach to PR.

5) 60–90 min: Failure rehearsal and recovery checklist
   - Ritual: simulate network partition or inject a 503 from the underlying runtime using the inject-failure CLI flag. Then exercise fallback policies (retry, model-variant, region).
   - Checklist: ensure idempotency keys included, backoff policy observed, and user-visible error is actionable.

Sample microcopy snippets (for UX teams)
- Auth failure: "We couldn't verify your API key. Try re-pasting it from your workspace settings."
- Latency warning in-app: "Responses are slower than usual. We are using a fallback model to keep things online."
- Cost ceiling hit: "Your request quota is near limit — consider upgrading or switching to a cached endpoint."

Telemetry and success signals to capture during the lab (minimal set)
- sdk_onramp_smoke (boolean) – did the initial smoke call succeed?
- sdk_onramp_latency_run (distribution) – p50/p95 latency of baseline run
- sdk_onramp_fallback (string) – fallback reason code (e.g., capacity, region, qps)
- sdk_onramp_quant_toggle (boolean) – whether user tried quant/config toggle
- sdk_onramp_completion (enum) – completed, abandoned, error

Example event payload (for engineers):
- event: sdk_onramp_latency_run
- properties: [p50_ms: 112, p95_ms: 380, model: open-mpt-7b/2025-03, region: us-west-2]

Short troubleshooting playbook (cheat sheet)
- 401 on smoke: check API key, workspace, and that the key is not scoped to a different team. Use HEAD /v1/auth/keys to validate.
- 409 region mismatch: ensure REDWOOD_REGION env var matches the Console's assigned default.
- Elevated latency during baseline: check client-side CPU (local batching can look bad if single-threaded), and ensure KV-cache warmup was done when testing long contexts.

Open questions and decisions to make (for product/pm)
- How opinionated should the default first-day config be? (Conservative: low-cost model + small tokens; Aggressive: show peak performance with optimized kernels.)
- Should the first-day lab auto-attach a temporary cost quota and telemetry opt-in, or require explicit consent?
- How long should cached examples/telemetry be retained in Console for a new signup? (7 days vs 30 days)

Suggested assets to ship with the lab
- repo: rdw-onramp-experiments (tiny CLI + node/python examples + load script) – include README with exact commands.
- Console view: a prebuilt dashboard template that pops up when a new workspace runs the smoke.
- PR templates: small checklist to attach to infra PRs that implements the ritual (e.g., pin model, include telemetry events).

Next steps (owner: Aisha)
- Build minimal repo and demo script (2 days)
- Sync with UX on microcopy and error states (1 meeting; invite Lena)
- Draft telemetry schema and short retention plan with Observability team (Samir)
- Run user test with two internal teams (SRE + product chat) and capture learnings (2 sprints)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive — the point is to teach small, repeatable actions that form a muscle memory.
- Feedback wanted: what is the minimal set of steps that would have fixed your last-onboarding ticket?

Raw links / scratch items
- Slack: #devexp-onramp
- Quick test script: ./scripts/onramp-bench --model open-mpt-7b --q 8bit-fast --duration 30
- Gist: sample telemetry event mappings (internal link)
